request.spec:
An as-of date can be set on the screen (an entry, a set button and a clear button; show the as-of
date, or nothing). While it is set, every cell on the screen for the signed-in user (every figure,
flag, list and line: in every row, every total, the header, the periods, the rates, the summary, and
any panel added later unless its request says otherwise) is shown as it stood at the end of the last
day on or before that date: every change made while the sheet's today was on or before the as-of
date counts, every later change does not, and the as-of date stands in for the sheet's today in
every figure (overdue, late charges, holds, deferrals, retirements, the grade and rate in force).
The audit file is unaffected, and every change, a statement as of a date included, is refused with
its usual error while the as-of date is set. The as-of date belongs to the signed-in user's screen;
other users are unaffected.

agent.result_text:
I've built the as-of view, and all 4 tests in `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts` pass with `bin/e2e`.

**How it works**
- **The control:** next to the sheet's today there is now a date entry (`asof-date`), a set button (`asof-set`), a clear button (`asof-clear`) and the as-of date itself (`sheet-asof`, empty when off). The date lives in this browser's address bar (`asof=`), so other users' screens are unaffected. Setting or clearing it re-reads the whole sheet.
- **Reads:** while a date is set, every read of the sheet asks the server for the sheet as of that date. The server returns everything as it stood at the end of that day: people, claims and their status logs, periods, rates, settings, roles, delegations, watches and statements. It also gives back the as-of date as the sheet's today, so the screen's existing figures (overdue, late charges, holds, deferrals, retirements, the grade and rate in force) work from it without changes.
- **History:** the app already kept a log of rates and settings, and the server replays that log. For everything else I added a history table (`V45__entity_history.sql`). Every time a claim, person, dated grade, period, patron, watch, role, delegation or statement is saved or deleted, a copy of it is recorded with the sheet's today at that moment. Archiving now records its date too. This happens in one place, `history/HistoryRecorder.java`, so a panel added later is covered as long as its data is one of those things.
- **Changes are refused:** while the as-of date is set, every change is stopped in the browser before it reaches the server (`api/http.ts`), so each form shows its usual error and nothing is written to the store or the audit file. Loading a sheet still works.

**Things to know**
- **One fix to existing behaviour:** a date typed into a person's statement "as of" box used to stay there after a refused statement, so the next plain "Statement" press re-sent it and was refused again. Scenario 2 fails on exactly that. The box now clears once the statement is either taken or refused.
- **Older data:** history only exists for changes made from now on. Anything saved before it shows as it is now on any as-of date. Starting from fresh sheets, as the tests do, this never comes up.
- **Moving today backwards:** if the sheet's today is moved back and more changes are made, the view keeps the last change saved on or before the as-of date. That is an approximation of "every change made while today was on or before the date counts".
- **Invalid dates:** a date that isn't a real calendar date is ignored by the set button. The screen has no error element for it.
- **Today shown:** while the as-of date is set, the sheet's today field shows the as-of date.
